view: AP portable (supine/semi-erect) frontal chest radiograph; L marker and up-arrow at image top right confirm conventional orientation (patient's left on image right)
technical_quality: Adequate but limited: portable AP with the patient/cassette tilted a few degrees (image rotated counter-clockwise), mild rotation, adequate inspiration (about 8 posterior ribs), upper abdomen included. Numerous external tubes/lines drape across both hemithoraces, shoulders and arms and partially obscure the lung fields.

devices.type: Probable central venous catheter (right neck / internal jugular approach), radiopaque hub over the right supraclavicular region
devices.location: Right neck/upper mediastinum, coursing down the right paratracheal region with tip projecting over the lower SVC / cavoatrial junction

devices.type: External tubing (IV / oxygen / monitoring tubing) forming loops
devices.location: Over the right shoulder, right axilla and right upper arm (patient's right, image left), continuing down along the right lateral chest wall

devices.type: External tube with radiopaque connector end
devices.location: Overlying the right mid zone near the right hilum (patient's right)

devices.type: Round radiopaque connector/electrode-type disc with attached tubing (looped tubing above it)
devices.location: Overlying the left mid zone / left anterior chest wall (patient's left, image right)

devices.type: External tubing running down the lateral chest wall with two radiopaque connector ends
devices.location: Left lateral chest wall to left upper abdomen / left flank, outside the rib cage (patient's left)

devices.type: Radiographic orientation markers (L marker and up-arrow) and AP/PORTABLE text labels
devices.location: Image top-right corner and top-left/top-right text

abnormalities.finding: Homogeneous increased opacity of the right lower zone with obscuration of the right hemidiaphragm and right heart border (silhouette sign) and blunting/obliteration of the right costophrenic angle, consistent with right pleural effusion layering posteriorly on the supine film
Diffuse veil-like reduced transparency of the entire right hemithorax compared with the left (layering effusion), extending into the right middle zone
Possible underlying right lower lobe atelectasis/consolidation within the dense right basal opacity (cannot be separated from effusion on this single view)
Cardiomediastinal silhouette appears prominent but cannot be reliably assessed on rotated portable AP projection; trachea midline; no endotracheal or nasogastric tube seen
Left lung essentially clear; left hemidiaphragm and gastric air bubble preserved; no definite left effusion or pneumothorax

description_zh: 攜帶式 AP 胸部 X 光，病人略有旋轉，胸壁上多條外在管路交錯投影於兩側胸部、肩部及上臂，影響判讀。右下肺野呈均質性密度增加，右側橫膈及右心緣模糊（silhouette sign），右側肋膈角消失，且整個右側胸廓透明度較左側減低，符合仰臥位右側肋膜積液呈層狀分布，範圍約 10 公分，不排除合併右下葉肺塌陷或實變。左肺大致清晰，左側橫膈與胃泡可見，未見明顯左側積液或氣胸。右頸部見疑似中心靜脈導管，尖端投影於上腔靜脈與右心房交界附近；未見胸管、肋膜引流管或氣管內管。
